items.title: Global Cybersecurity Outlook 2026
items.description: Organizations with a process to assess AI tool security before deployment rose from 37% in 2025 to 64% in 2026, indicating rapid maturation of AI governance practices year over year.

items.title: Share of organizations assessing AI tool security nearly doubled
items.description: Organizations with a process to assess AI tool security before deployment rose from 37% in 2025 to 64% in 2026, indicating rapid maturation of AI governance practices year over year.

items.title: Perceived increase in cyber risks over the past year
items.description: Survey respondents rated which cyber risks increased in 2025. AI vulnerabilities (87%) and cyber-enabled fraud and phishing (77%) lead a broad-based perception of escalating threats.

items.title: Year-over-year strategy shifts due to geopolitical volatility
items.description: The share of organizations changing their cybersecurity strategy because of geopolitical volatility declined from 93% in 2023 to 66% in 2026, suggesting the initial adaptation wave has passed even as geopolitics remains the top risk factor.

items.title: Reversal in top genAI concern: data leaks now lead
items.description: In 2026, data leaks via genAI rose to 34% (from 22% in 2025) while advancement of adversarial capabilities fell to 29% (from 47% in 2025) - a striking reversal in the top genAI cybersecurity concern.

items.title: Cyber resilience self-assessment 2024-2026
items.description: Organizations reporting resilience that exceeds requirements doubled from 9% in 2025 to 19% in 2026, while those reporting insufficient resilience held steady, indicating concentrated improvement at the top end.

items.title: Regional confidence in national response to critical infrastructure attacks
items.description: Confidence varies sharply across regions. MENA respondents express the highest confidence in their country's ability to protect critical infrastructure (84%), while Latin America and the Caribbean trail at just 13%.

items.title: Most common cyber-enabled fraud types reported by respondents
items.description: Phishing/vishing/smishing (62%), invoice or payment fraud (37%) and identity theft (32%) lead the categories of cyber-enabled fraud experienced personally or in respondents' networks.

items.title: Regional prevalence of cyber-enabled fraud exposure
items.description: Sub-Saharan Africa leads exposure with 82% of respondents reporting they or their network were affected, followed by North America at 79%. East Asia & Pacific trails at 59%, reflecting differing fraud ecosystems.

items.title: CEOs' top genAI security concerns
items.description: CEOs identify data leaks (30%) and the advancement of adversarial capabilities (28%) as the most significant security concerns related to generative AI - the two risks stand clearly above technical security (15%) and governance complexity (13%).

items.title: Top AI-for-cybersecurity use cases
items.description: Among the 77% of organizations using AI for cybersecurity, phishing detection (52%) and intrusion/anomaly response (46%) lead use cases, followed by automated security operations (43%) and user-behaviour analytics (40%).

items.title: Greatest challenges to organizational cyber resilience
items.description: The rapidly evolving threat landscape (61%), third-party and supply chain vulnerabilities (46%), and the cybersecurity skills shortage (45%) are the top three barriers to building resilience in 2026.

items.title: Technologies with the greatest cybersecurity impact in next 12 months
items.description: AI/ML tops the list at 94%, far ahead of cloud (61%), quantum (37%), autonomous systems (26%), decentralized tech (20%), and space technologies (9%) - confirming AI and cloud as the dominant focus areas.

items.title: How organizations address supply chain cyber risk
items.description: While 66% of organizations assess supplier security maturity and 65% involve security in procurement, only 27% simulate cyber incidents with partners and 33% comprehensively map their ecosystem - showing checkbox compliance over dynamic management.

items.title: AI-enabled cybersecurity tool adoption by company size and sector
items.description: AI for cybersecurity is dominated by large enterprises (93% adoption, >$5.5B revenue) and medium firms (83%), while small companies (78%), the public sector (45%) and NGOs (70%) lag - deepening cyber inequity.

items.title: Regional cyber skills gap: LATAM and Sub-Saharan Africa hit hardest
items.description: 65% of organizations in Latin America and the Caribbean and 63% in Sub-Saharan Africa report missing critical people and skills for cybersecurity objectives, compared to 35% in South Asia and 37% in Europe & Central Asia.

items.title: Largest organizations have re-tooled cyber strategy for geopolitics
items.description: 91% of the largest organizations (>100,000 employees) have changed their cybersecurity strategies due to geopolitical volatility, compared to 59% of those with under 1,000 employees - showing scale-driven divergence in resilience investment.

items.title: AI vulnerabilities are the fastest-growing cyber risk
items.description: 87% of respondents identified AI-related vulnerabilities as the fastest-growing cyber risk over the course of 2025, ranking the category ahead of cyber-enabled fraud, supply chain disruption and ransomware.

items.title: Public sector lags private on cyber resilience
items.description: 23% of public-sector organizations report having insufficient cyber-resilience capabilities, compared to just 11% in the private sector - a structural inequity highlighted by recent infrastructure incidents.

items.title: AI named top driver of cybersecurity change
items.description: AI is anticipated to be the most significant driver of change in cybersecurity in the year ahead, according to 94% of survey respondents. The Forum frames AI as both a force multiplier for defenders and a catalyst for attackers in 2026.

items.title: Geopolitical attacks lead cyber risk mitigation strategies
items.description: 64% of organizations are accounting for geopolitically motivated cyberattacks - such as disruption of critical infrastructure or espionage - making geopolitics the top factor influencing risk mitigation in 2026.

items.title: Cyber-enabled fraud is reaching households
items.description: 73% of respondents reported that they or someone in their network had been personally affected by cyber-enabled fraud in the past 12 months, with phishing/vishing/smishing the most common attack type (62%).

items.title: AI is now standard in defensive operations
items.description: 77% of organizations have adopted AI for cybersecurity, primarily for phishing detection (52%), intrusion and anomaly response (46%), and user-behaviour analytics (40%).

items.title: OT security barely reaches the board
items.description: Only 16% of organizations with industrial environments report OT security issues to their boards, and just 20% maintain a dedicated OT security team - underscoring persistent governance gaps in cyber-physical security.

items.title: Most security leaders see regulations as effective
items.description: 74% of respondents hold a positive view of the effectiveness of cyber-related regulations - citing board awareness (58%) and posture improvement (55%) as top benefits, even as multinationals struggle with consistency.

items.title: Jaguar Land Rover cyberattack triggered $2.5B UK economic loss
items.description: The August 2025 cyberattack on Jaguar Land Rover halted production for five weeks, affected 5,000+ suppliers, drove a ~25% revenue drop and an estimated GBP 1.9 billion ($2.5B) in wider UK economic losses. Direct cyber-related costs reached GBP 196M ($260M).

items.title: Average significant UK cyberattack costs ~$250K
items.description: Per UK government research cited by WEF, the average significant cyberattack costs businesses nearly GBP 195,000 ($250,000), which scales to an estimated GBP 14.7B ($19.4B) in annual economic losses nationally.

items.title: State-linked crypto-exchange breach: $1.5B in losses
items.description: In 2025, a major crypto-exchange breach attributed to a state-linked threat group resulted in losses exceeding $1.5 billion, with nearly a fifth of stolen funds rapidly converted into unrecoverable assets.

items.title: 99% of international data traffic flows through undersea cables
items.description: Per ITU Secretary-General Doreen Bogdan-Martin, 99% of international data traffic flows through undersea cables, yet only 18% of organizations account for undersea cables in cyber risk mitigation.

items.title: Operation Serengeti 2.0: $97.4M recovered, 1,209 arrests
items.description: INTERPOL's Operation Serengeti 2.0 - coordinated with 18 African countries and the UK to tackle ransomware, online scams and BEC - led to 1,209 arrests and the recovery of $97.4 million in 2025.

items.title: Lumma Infostealer disruption: 394,000 infected machines
items.description: Europol and Microsoft jointly disrupted the Lumma infostealer ecosystem, affecting 394,000 infected machines and seizing 1,300+ malicious domains - one of the largest 2025 infostealer takedowns.

items.title: Norwegian hydropower dam hack released 500 L/s for 4 hours
items.description: In April 2025, a Norwegian hydropower dam was hacked, opening a floodgate and releasing 500 litres of water per second for four hours - described by officials as a deliberate act of sabotage on critical infrastructure.

items.title: Cybersecurity is a frontier of collaboration
items.description: From the Executive Summary, the WEF frames cybersecurity as inherently collaborative even in a fragmented world - a recurring theme across the 2026 outlook.
items.quote: "Cybersecurity is a frontier where collaboration remains not only possible, but powerful - a reminder that, even amid fragmentation, economic strain and uncertainty, collective action can drive progress for all."

items.title: IBM CEO on agentic AI for defenders
items.description: Arvind Krishna, CEO of IBM, on the necessity of using every available tool - including agentic AI - to defend against criminal abuse of cyber infrastructure.
items.quote: "Criminals are always willing to use all possible ways to get access to value, much of which is contained in the cyber infrastructure. Consequently, to stay ahead, those of us who defend must use every tool at our disposal - which now includes agentic AI."

items.title: Low confidence in national cyber preparedness rising
items.description: 31% of survey participants express lack of confidence in their nation's ability to respond effectively to major cyber incidents, up from 26% last year, signaling growing uncertainty around critical infrastructure protection.

items.title: Supply chain risk now top barrier for large companies
items.description: 65% of large companies by revenue cite third-party and supply chain vulnerabilities as their greatest challenge to cyber resilience, up from 54% in 2025 - reflecting heightened sensitivity after major 2025 incidents.
